evidence: Kew/POWO accepts Conoclinium coelestinum and lists Texas within its native range.
Hays County — the project Hays County native-source list includes C. coelestinum.
Travis County — Texas Wildbuds documents C. coelestinum at St. Edward's Park, Austin, and treats the species as Texas-native.

Williamson County — the University of Texas Plant Resources Center provides a dedicated Williamson County treatment for C. coelestinum and Texas Wildbuds independently documents it at Lake Georgetown.
target_zone_range.guardrail: Purola Preserve in north Hays County lists its own C. coelestinum population as intentionally introduced from nearby Hill Country material. That site record is explicitly excluded from the native-range count.

morphology.look_here_first: Start with the leaves and head type: opposite triangular/deltate 3-veined leaves below a flat-topped misty cluster of tiny blue-violet heads made entirely of disk florets—there are no ray florets.
diagnostic_traits: rhizomatous perennial herb, often forming colonies and sometimes rooting at buried/decumbent nodes
leaves opposite and decussate, simple and petiolate
leaf blades triangular to deltate, serrate to serrate-dentate, usually strongly 3-veined from the base
foliage and stems bear short and glandular hairs but are not aromatic
inflorescence a terminal/axillary flat-topped to domed array of many small heads
heads are discoid, with many bisexual blue-violet disk florets and no ray florets
involucre with roughly 20–35 narrow phyllaries in 2–3 series
fruit a small ribbed cypsela topped by a pappus of capillary bristles

confusers.separator: Both have opposite leaves and flat-topped clusters of all-disk heads. White snakeroot has white heads and broader, coarsely toothed long-petioled leaves; blue mistflower has blue-violet heads and smaller triangular/deltate leaves.
Gregg's/palmleaf mistflower has much more deeply dissected foliage and is associated with drier calcareous habitats; blue mistflower has broad triangular leaves and usually moister sites.
Several bonesets have white heads and narrower or differently arranged leaves; use head color, leaf shape/venation, and phyllaries rather than the fluffy appearance alone.

diagnostic_roles: single discoid head showing no rays
